newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on crush talk despite Japan.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on crush talk despite Japan.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower on talk CanAmera Foods will shut a Prairie canola crush plant on Thursday due to poor crush margins, traders said.

"I heard CanAmera's going to close one of the western crush plants today," a trader said. CanAmera did not return calls. It ceased canola crushing at its largest plant in Ontario last week. Volume was 7,550 lots, or 151,000 tonnes.

"Japan bought 15,000 tonnes overnight. Nobody's sure what to do, the charts are compressing," a trader said. Jan-Mar spread at $2.10, Mar-May $0.50. January futures crush margin rose to -36.93 from -38.99 Wednesday.
January canola fell $1.40 to $405 and March dipped $0.10 to $407.60. January flax rose $1 to $358.50 on commercial demand. About 200 Jan-Mar spread at $4 and UGG bought, traders said.

March feed wheat lost $0.70 to $169.80 as Alberta Wheat Pool sold, traders said. About 200 Mar-May spread at $1. Forty oat contracts ended down US$2 to US$5 at US$116 in May while October finished at US$114 October.
February western barley fell $2.30 at $137.70, March lost $2.30 to $137.20 as Midland Walwyn sold half of the 2,000 contracts traded, traders said.
UGG sold five October peas up US$1 to US$204, sold 80 July down US$5 to US$188.90 and 100 October down US$2 to US$184, traders said.
(Values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats).
